name: The Seven Holy Brothers, and Saints Rufina and Secunda
history: Two groups of early Roman martyrs kept together on this day. The seven brothers, by tradition sons of Saint Felicity, died under Antoninus Pius in the second century; Rufina and Secunda, two sisters who had vowed themselves to God, died under Valerian in the third. The brothers were already honoured on 10 July in the Roman calendar of 354.
life: The old Roman list of the burials of martyrs, compiled in 354, records on this day seven martyrs buried in four different cemeteries around the city: Felix and Philip, Martial, Vitalis and Alexander, Silvanus, and Januarius. A later account made them the seven sons of Saint Felicity, a widow who encouraged each of them to die bravely before she died herself, like the mother in the Book of Maccabees. Whatever their family ties, their cult is ancient and well founded. Rufina and Secunda, according to their tradition, were sisters of a Christian family in Rome who refused marriage in order to belong to Christ, and who were arrested when they would not deny Him. They were put to death on the Via Cornelia, outside the city, around 257. A bishopric near Rome later bore Rufina’s name.
prayerTo: Holy brothers and holy sisters, martyrs of Rome, you encouraged one another to be faithful to the end. Pray for brothers and sisters in every family, for mothers who hand on the faith, and for all consecrated virgins. Help my family to strengthen one another in Christ. Amen.
penance: Pray today for your own brothers and sisters, or those who have been like them to you, and contact one of them.
meditation: Seven brothers, two sisters, one Lord. How do you help those closest to you to be faithful?
prayer: Grant, we beseech You, almighty God, that we who know how courageously Your holy Martyrs have confessed the faith, may experience their goodness as they intercede for us with You. Through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
prayerSource: Collect of the day, Roman Missal of 1962
